## Three layers in one box

::: {.layers}
::: {.layer .perceive}
<div class="eyebrow c-perceive">Perceive</div>
### It sees the whole instrument
Live's object model, read at runtime: 47 types, 922 members. Observers report what you change by hand, so Claude knows when you nudged a fader.
:::
::: {.layer .reason}
<div class="eyebrow c-reason">Reason</div>
### It looks before it guesses
A skill teaches the model how Live's paths are shaped. When "cutoff" finds nothing, it searches Drift's parameters and finds LP Freq, then reads the range before writing.
:::
::: {.layer .act}
<div class="eyebrow c-act">Act</div>
### It writes with undo
Thirty tools, and batched writes that undo as one step where Live allows it. Anything that removes, clears or crops waits for confirmation.
:::
:::

## Why this one

Every other Ableton MCP server hand-writes one command per feature, so what Claude can reach is whatever someone found time to type. Sideman exposes Live's own object model, the same `path` / `get` / `set` / `call` contract Max for Live uses. Any property Live has is reachable without shipping new code.

**Everything, not a menu.** Every parameter on every native device, every clip property, every mixer control. Coverage is measured against a running Live, not counted from a README. The largest command-list server stops at 128.

**It sees what you do.** Nudge a fader, rename a track, drop a clip with your hands, and Claude knows. Nothing else in the field reports changes you make yourself.

**⌘Z still works.** Edits land as real undo steps. A batch of renames, colours and time signatures collapses into one. Tempo, volume and device parameters keep their own step, so occasionally it is ⌘Z twice.

**It asks before it deletes.** Anything that removes, clears or crops waits for confirmation. Your Set is not in version control, and the server behaves like it knows that.

**New Live, nothing to update.** The object model is read from Live at runtime. When Live adds a function, it is reachable the day you upgrade.

## Three things you'd actually say

> Give me a 4-bar house loop. Chords, bass, drums. Name the tracks and colour them.

A third MIDI track created, all three named and coloured, six writes in one undo step. Drift loaded from the browser. Four-bar clips written, kick on every quarter, hats offbeat with alternating velocity. Scene 1 fired.

> Open the filter over the loop. Closed at the start, wide by bar 4.

Searches Drift's parameters by name. "Cutoff" finds nothing, so it looks instead of guessing and finds LP Freq. Reads the range, writes a rising sweep one step a bar, then reads the envelope back so you can check it before it plays.

> I was dragging the tempo just now. Where did I land?

Observers were already watching. Tempo 123.5 → 122.5 → 123.5, and a fader on track 1 moved to 0.72. Those are real events from the tutorial run.

## Install

**Musicians:** download the `.pkg` from the [releases page](https://github.com/slegroux/sideman/releases). It installs into your home folder, needs no password and brings its own Python. It is not yet notarized, so the first time macOS will refuse a double-click: right-click the `.pkg` → Open → Open, or on macOS 15 and later, System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. The one step no installer can do for you: Preferences → Link, Tempo & MIDI → Control Surface → AbletonLOM. Then restart Live once and your Claude session once.

**Developers:** clone, make a Python 3.11 venv, run the install script, pick AbletonLOM as a Control Surface in Live's preferences, register with Claude Code, then restart Live and your Claude session.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/slegroux/sideman && cd sideman
uv venv --python 3.11 .venv
VIRTUAL_ENV=.venv uv pip install -e .
./scripts/install.sh
claude mcp add --scope user sideman -- "$PWD/.venv/bin/python" -m mcp_server.server
```

The [full install guide](https://slegroux.github.io/sideman/#install), the [tutorial](https://github.com/slegroux/sideman/blob/main/docs/TUTORIAL.md) and the [tool reference](https://github.com/slegroux/sideman/blob/main/docs/TOOLS.md) live with the code.

## Works with

| | |
|---|---|
| Ableton Live | Live 12, any edition. It is a Remote Script, so Max for Live is not required. |
| Computer | macOS. Windows untested. |
| Assistant | Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client. |
| Plugins | Every parameter of every native device and rack. VST/AU parameters you have exposed with Live's Configure button. |
| Network | None. Talks to Live on localhost, on its own port, so it coexists with other Ableton servers. |
